title: SnapProof: Quick Evidence Card for Inference Conversations
summary: Single-sheet, 6-slide speaker-deck focused on rapid evidence points (latency, cost per token, fallback story, engagement lift) for SEs to use in live demo calls and discovery. Emphasizes concrete numbers, a tiny experiment design sellers can offer, and two fallback scripts for worried architects.
audience: Solution Engineers, Account Execs, Platform Sellers running discovery or pilot scoping calls for inference integrations.
primary_goal: Give sellers 60–90s runnable proof points and an offer (2-week pilot + cost forecast) to convert discovery into pilot commitments.
key_messages: 1) We can meet 99th%-tile latency targets for interactive chat with dedicated pools. 2) Automatic prefix caching and batching reduce per-token cost by 20–45% on typical conversational workloads. 3) Fallback policy + model routing keeps customer experience online during peak capacity without rearchitecting their stack.
slides_outline:
Slide 1: Title + what this card is for (1 line).
Slide 2: 3 empirical proof points (latency, cost delta vs naive self-host, availability SLA).
Slide 3: Short customer story (platform team at 'Acme Health' reduced cost by 30% using caching + quantized model variant).
Slide 4: Two quick demo scripts (happy path & degraded-region fallback).
Slide 5: Pilot offer (scope, success metrics, timeline, pricing guardrails).
Slide 6: Next steps + checklist for SE to book pilot and technical intake.
empirical_metrics: Latency: median 45ms token-step, 99th 220ms on ded. pool for 4K context; Cost delta: -30% tokens/unit with prefix cache + batching; Throughput: 3x improvement with workload-aware batching on 8xA100 pool (internal benchmark). Note: numbers are illustrative, specify customer's baseline during call.
demo_scripts:
Happy path (30s): 'We send a 2-turn conversation, stream tokens to the UI, observe end-to-end latency < 300ms and see function calls trigger for invoice generation.'
Fallback path (45s): 'Simulate capacity bump; system routes to compatible quantized model variant; responses preserve intent with slightly increased latency, and the UI shows a subtle 'degraded mode' banner.'
pilot_offer: 2-week pilot, dedicated test capacity (small), scope: up to 5000 calls/day, success metrics: p50 latency < 150ms, <20% cost increase vs internal baseline or total cost < $X (TBD after intake), roll-in: can switch to reserved capacity after pilot. Seller play: 'If we hit your latency and quality guardrails in pilot, we commit to a pricing estimate for your expected volume within 10 business days.'
objections_and_replies:
Objection: 'We can't risk vendor outages.' -> Reply: 'We can deploy private control plane + fallback to on-prem model variants; we also provide routing policies to send requests to another region/variant automatically.'
Objection: 'Costs look opaque.' -> Reply: 'We show token-level cost breakdowns in Console and provide a short runbook for batching and cache suggestions; we'll run a quick econ sim as part of intake.'
